title: Stuffed Peppers
subtitle: Bell peppers filled with spiced rice and beef, baked until tender
excerpt: Red and yellow peppers halved and filled with a mixture of beef mince, rice, tomato, and herbs, then baked until the pepper softens and the filling is cooked through. A satisfying one-dish supper.

recipe.sourceNotes: Stuffed peppers appear across Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, and Central European cooking. The technique of filling a hollowed vegetable with a rice and meat mixture is shared across Turkish dolma, Italian peperoni ripieni, and Hungarian töltött paprika. This British-adapted version uses red and yellow peppers for sweetness, a simple spiced mince filling, and rice cooked in the filling itself during baking.

recipeTools.notes: Large enough to hold 8 pepper halves upright.

content.text: Use long-grain or basmati rice rather than risotto rice: it stays separate rather than turning sticky. The rice goes in raw and cooks in the steam inside the pepper during baking. Cover the tin tightly with foil for the first 30 minutes so the steam cannot escape.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, paprika, and cumin and cook for 1 minute. Add the mince and fry for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the tomato puree, tinned tomatoes, salt, and pepper. Add the uncooked rice. Mix well. The filling should be saucy: add 100 ml of water if it looks dry. Remove from the heat.
Sit the pepper halves cut-side up in a large roasting tin. Divide the filling evenly between the 8 halves. Cover the tin tightly with foil. Bake for 30 minutes.
Remove the foil. Sprinkle the grated cheese over the top of each pepper. Bake uncovered for a further 10 minutes until the cheese is golden and the peppers are tender. Scatter with parsley and serve.
